summary: C. R. Agnew Jr., writing as Director of the National Campground Owners Association and Member of the Executive Committee of the Ski Touring Council, strongly opposes expanded ORV use on public lands. He argues that healthful non-motorized recreation (hiking, ski touring, backpacking, camping, fishing, canoeing, etc.) should be promoted while motorized activities are discouraged, that ORV users should be accommodated on private rather than public lands, and that stringent controls are needed to prevent environmental damage, noise/air pollution, and harm to other recreationists.

statement.text:
C. R. AGNEW JR. 357 ROUND HILL ROAD BREENWICH, CONN. 06830
203 869-1368
July 19, 1972
Honorable Rogers C. B. Morton, Secretary Department of the Interior Washington, D. C.
Dear Mr. Morton:
70
My affiliations are: Director, National Campground Owners Association; Member, Executive Committee, Ski Touring Council. I comment on your letter of May 5th, 1972 and the Draft Environmental Statement.
1. Healthful recreation activities should be promoted, motorized activities should be discouraged. The President issued Order 11644 by virtue of authority vested in him by the Constitution. He is empowered to promote regulations for the benefit of the American people.
It is submitted that the healthful outdoor sports and recreation activities of benefit to the minds, bodies and spirits of the American people are the non-motorized sports of: hiking, ski touring, backpacking and camping, fishing, canoeing, sailing, horseback riding.
These activities contribute to the healthful growth and development of Americans. By the opposite token motorized activities do not essentially foster and promote body, mental and spiritual health. Indeed in some instances motorized activities are counter productive to healthful recreation activities and detract from healthful recreation of others.
2. Motorized recreation activities should be undertaken on private lands and by arrangement with private landowners.
Owners of off-road vehicles are not poverty stricken. Government has no obligation to subsidize these vehicle owners, nor to allow them to use vast areas of our public lands.
The experience of the compground industry in the past 15 years can be cited. Formerly, government provided the bulk of campsites. In the past 15 years a longe private or reproved industry has risen. Today the great bulk of American convers - 705 - are accomplated at private campgrounds. Government arenaies have greatly reduced expenditures for construction of campgrounds.
It has been demonstrated that family campers and toruists are not basically interested in the wilderness and nature. They wish to vacation amid conventional man-made surroundings. They wish to bring the commercial comforts of home to the wilderness. If given the chance they would commefcially exploit our wilderness treasures.

There is no need to turn over vast areas of public lands for the use of off-road vehicles. Users can be accommodated by arrangement with private landowners.
3. Stringent Controls Urged for Off-road Vehicles.
a. The use of ORVs is to be discouraged for health reasons. The throwing open of large areas of public lands to them will encourage the growth and development of the industry. Strict controls will hold back industry expansion. 
b. If areas are now thrown open to ORVs the following will ensue: 
i. Environmental damage from operation of machines.
ii. Noise and air pollution will occur.
iii. The pollution will seriously detract from healthful ourdoor recreation pursuits of persons who enjoy the peace and serenity of wilderness type areas.
iv. Once a pattern is set for ORVs it will be difficult or impossible to reverse it later if we find that we are overwhelmed with motor driven vehicles.
Ray Cigner.

C. R. Agnew Jr.
